credentials.description: client_id of the environment (sandbox: developer account dashboard; production: Settings → API Keys, v4)

parameters.name: X-Trace-Id
parameters.description: A unique identifier to track this operation. It must be between 12 and 255 characters in length.

parameters.name: X-Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique identifier to prevent duplicate requests. It must be between 12 and 255 characters in length.

example_prompt: Refund all or part of a successful Flutterwave charge and track the refund to completion.

charge_id.description: ID of the charge to refund

data.description: A refund of a previously created charge

charge_id.description: ID of the charge tied to this refund

message.description: Present on 401/403/409 bodies; the 400 body has none.

type.description: Error category. Generic: REQUEST_NOT_VALID, UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, RESOURCE_CONFLICT, UNPROCESSABLE, INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR; or a domain type (see code).

code.description: String. Generic 10400/10401/10403/10404/10409/10422/10500, or a domain code documented for this endpoint: 1402400 REFUND_AMOUNT_INVALID (more than the charge), 1403400 REFUND_CREATION_FAILED (charge still pending), 1404400 REFUND_ALREADY_COMPLETED.

gotchas: Auth: one token server for both environments — the docs' Multi-Environment Integrations example sends either environment's credentials to https://idp.flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token, and Authentication says "This process applies to both the sandbox and production environments. Make sure to use the correct credentials for each environment to obtain a valid token." "Each token is valid for **10 minutes**"; "We recommend refreshing the token at least one minute before it expires." Cache the token. Sandbox: "We archive your test data after 30 days."

Headers: send X-Idempotency-Key on this POST. Docs (Idempotency): "For all `POST` endpoints, include an idempotency key in the request header (`X-Idempotency-Key`)." The API reference marks it optional; the headers guide lists it under 'Mandatory API Headers'. A reused key replays the first response ("the response will include the header `X-Idempotency-Cache-Hit: true`"), so reuse the key when retrying the same operation and use a new one for a new operation. X-Trace-Id is optional. For both: "It must be a string using only alphanumeric ASCII characters." "Its length should be between 12 and 255 characters." The idempotency page also says "We recommend using a **UUID** string as your idempotency key": strip the UUID's hyphens to satisfy both.
Body: charge_id, amount (decimal), reason (duplicate | fraudulent | requested_by_customer | expired_uncaptured_charge), meta. Only successful charges can be refunded (1403400 otherwise).

Docs (Refunds): "To initiate a part or partial refund, ensure that the refund amount is smaller than the transaction amount." Several partial refunds are allowed on one charge; their total can't exceed the charge amount (the guide's wording is "equal to"). "The refund will be deducted from your available balance or the next settlement."

Lifecycle: Docs (Refunds): "When a Refund is first initiated, its status is `new`." then pending, then succeeded or failed. The API's enum also has completed (the guide's own create example returns it), cancelled and requires_action. Treat succeeded / completed as refunded, failed / cancelled as not refunded, and requires_action as undocumented: escalate instead of polling forever. Treat any 2xx as created (the guide's sample is labelled 200 OK).
Final status: refund.completed webhook or get_refund. Open question: the guide mentions a `callbackurl` body field that the API reference does not define.

Errors: {"status":"failed","error":{"type","code","message","validation_errors"}}; error.code is a string and 400s carry validation_errors[{field_name,message}]. Besides the generic codes (10400 REQUEST_NOT_VALID, 10401, 10403 FORBIDDEN, 10404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, 10409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT, 10422 UNPROCESSABLE, 10500) the error table documents these for this endpoint: 1402400 REFUND_AMOUNT_INVALID (more than the charge), 1403400 REFUND_CREATION_FAILED (charge still pending), 1404400 REFUND_ALREADY_COMPLETED. Branch on error.type / error.code, not on the HTTP status alone. Docs (Errors): "The current limit is 500 API requests per minute." A 429 can come back as a non-JSON page ("HTML error pages such as `Cloudflare 1015 responses`"): parse error bodies defensively and back off exponentially with jitter.
open_questions: Token URL: the PHP sample of Authentication uses https://keycloak.dev-flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token; its curl and JavaScript samples and the Multi-Environment example use https://idp.flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token, which this spec follows.
